Stage 1 component distributions. The figure uses layer 1 molecular data. Facets show components
1-2 in decomposition order; stored densities summarize sample-coordinate distributions; rugs
mark sample coordinates; dotted vertical lines mark zero. Categorical metadata is shown by
density fills, outlines, and rug colours. Baseline stems additionally use line type and height.
The analysis unit is independent biological observation; the design is cross-sectional; the
estimand is the descriptive distribution of sample coordinates. No component-selection
threshold is applied. This descriptive gallery does not rank or nominate a biological
coordinate.
Stage 1 component distributions. The figure uses layer 1 molecular data. Facets show components
1-2 in decomposition order; stored densities summarize sample-coordinate distributions; rugs
mark sample coordinates; dotted vertical lines mark zero. Continuous metadata is shown by rug
colour. Baseline stems additionally use width and height. The analysis unit is independent
biological observation; the design is cross-sectional; the estimand is the descriptive
distribution of sample coordinates. No component-selection threshold is applied. This
descriptive gallery does not rank or nominate a biological coordinate.
Stage 1 decomposition coordinates. The figure uses layer 1, layer 2 molecular data. Facets
identify molecular layers; points show component 1 sample coordinates rank-ordered within each
layer; the dotted horizontal line marks zero. Point colours and point shapes encode categorical
planted group. The subtitle reports the stored synthetic ground-truth angle for component 1.
The analysis unit is independent biological observation; the design is cross-sectional; the
estimand is the descriptive sample coordinate on component 1. No component-selection threshold
is applied. This display does not select a component or establish biological interpretation.
Stage 1 decomposition coordinates. The figure uses layer 1, layer 2 molecular data. Facets
identify molecular layers; points show component 1 sample coordinates rank-ordered within each
layer; the dotted horizontal line marks zero. Point colours and point sizes encode continuous
observed time. The subtitle reports the stored synthetic ground-truth angle for component 1.
The analysis unit is independent biological observation; the design is cross-sectional; the
estimand is the descriptive sample coordinate on component 1. No component-selection threshold
is applied. This display does not select a component or establish biological interpretation.
Density-derived quasi-potential landscape. The figure uses layer 1, layer 2 molecular data. The
black curve shows U(x) = -log p(x), derived from the stored density estimate for component 1.
Rug colour identifies categorical planted group; baseline stem type and height provide
redundant encodings. Critical-point symbols and barrier-height segments are omitted. The
analysis unit is independent biological observation; the design is cross-sectional; the
estimand is the density-derived quasi-potential along the selected component. No calibrated
critical-point or barrier threshold is applied. The landscape is an exploratory description and
does not by itself establish a biological state transition.

Density-derived quasi-potential landscape. The figure uses layer 1, layer 2 molecular data. The
black curve shows U(x) = -log p(x), derived from the stored density estimate for component 1.
Rug colour identifies categorical planted group; baseline stem width and height provide
redundant encodings. Exploratory downward triangles mark stored wells; symbols are offset from
their stored coordinates and linked by dashed stems. Exploratory upward triangles mark stored
barriers; symbols are offset from their stored coordinates and linked by dashed stems. Dotted
vertical segments show point-estimate barrier heights. The analysis unit is independent
biological observation; the design is cross-sectional; the estimand is the density-derived
quasi-potential along the selected component. Critical-point classifications and barrier
heights are point estimates without uncertainty. No calibrated critical-point or barrier
threshold is applied. The landscape is an exploratory description and does not by itself
establish a biological state transition.
